$comment: Provenance for the run records in this directory, and the binding that makes it checkable. A conformance result is a statement about an implementation under test, so it has to name which implementation produced it; the record files carry only the outcome, and the two revision-2 records are otherwise indistinguishable. checkerSourceDigest is a deterministic hash of Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and src/**, computed by scripts/checker_digest.py, rather than a commit SHA, which cannot name the commit that carries it. reportSha256 binds this file to the records, and scripts/validate-index.py checks the whole thing in CI so a swapped report or drifted metadata fails rather than passing quietly. Reading this file is required to learn which checker produced a record: the records do not carry it themselves.

records.note: Blind first run: no vector-driven fixes.
The unchanged revision-1 build against revision 2. This is the revision boundary; the six diverging vectors are named in the record.
The revision-2 corpus under the merged checker. Superseded as the continuously verified record by suite-revision-3.json; kept because the 132 to 138 boundary is only readable against it.

First run against revision 3, by the unchanged revision-2 checker. Its reason-map membership rule was derived from the spec text and predates bad-731 and bad-732 by about an hour and three quarters, so the two new vectors met a rule that was already there rather than driving it.

Revision 5 pins the two things the v0.6 text left open, encoding and nesting depth. The unchanged revision-3 checker scored 148/149 against it, missing only bad-741: this implementation had picked 256 where the text now says 128, and counted depth per parsed value where the text now says per open container. Both halves are fixed here. The constant alone would also have scored 149/149, which is why the boundary the corpus does not reach is pinned in the parser's own tests instead.

Revision 6 adds the depth boundary pair and the noncharacter pair. The unchanged revision-5 checker scored 151/153 against it: ok-036 and bad-742 passed on the container-branch counter already in place, and bad-743 and bad-744 did not, because this checker did not implement the RFC 7493 section 2.1 noncharacter exclusion the revision makes normative. A directed fix, not a blind run: the rule was stated before this checker was run. Repinned 2026-08-01 from 7098f4e6b7d04c8394969ed81b4025d4d9038324, which the suite's author rewrote out of reachability on 2026-07-29 while stripping unreachable blobs. The replacement carries the identical root tree 71365c5aa24432c3e3c246b80f1e65183527852f, so the corpus this record was made against is unchanged to the byte; only the name that reaches it is. The old commit still answers the API but is absent from a fresh clone, which is the access path a reproduction actually uses. Marked not continuously verified from 2026-08-03: the working tree has moved to the v0.7 build, so this record's digest names a build the tree no longer carries.

Blind first run. Source not recoverable; see sourceUnrecoverable. The record file's indeterminateParity and $comment were appended by hand when the denominator was corrected, so the file's shape is not one this binary emits.
records.sourceUnrecoverable: The blind build was never committed on its own: 46ca0ee carries both the v0.7 implementation and this number, so no tree in this repository hashes to the build that produced 179/232. The figure is attested by the pin record and the commit ordering and is not independently reproducible, including by its author. Breaks PROTOCOL-v0.7.md rule 6; a future blind pass commits the build before running it.

records.note: Directed: followed a spec diff already read, and for bad-902 an adversarial review of this implementation. Reproduces exactly from the working tree. Carries per-vector condition codes from this revision. No reasonParity is published here: the codes introduced in #8 were taken from the corpus's own vocabulary, so a figure scored against that vocabulary measures how completely the naming was aligned rather than whether the condition was identified independently. See README.

Directed. Implements the universal partner in the coverage-validity list of spec 237f83b9: every carried record binding to this run whose aeeKind names a covering kind satisfies every constraint of that kind. The prior build scored 234 of 248 on this same pin, missing fourteen (bad-1001..1011, bad-1013, bad-1015, bad-1016), because it was written against 23bee586 where that clause did not exist. Build committed before the run, which is the rule-6 remedy v0.7-RUN.md promised after the blind run breached it.
records.reasonParityNote: Condition codes for the new class were chosen from the spec text without reading the corpus's declared codes, so the new refusals report carried-record-invalid, which is this implementation's name and not necessarily the corpus's. The absolute figure is unchanged from the 68/178 this build scored before the fix; the denominator grew by the fourteen newly refused.
records.checkerCommitNote: Names the squash-merge commit on main, not the pre-merge commit that carried the build. Both trees produce checkerSourceDigest 4757a94a, but only this one is reachable from a fresh clone, which is the access path a reproduction actually uses. The pre-merge SHA still answers the GitHub API and would look fine to anyone checking it that way, which is what makes the trap quiet. Same lesson as the revision-6 suite repin in this index, applied to the checker side rather than the suite side.

Placeholder until this branch squash-merges; repoint to the commit on main, per the trap the revision-25 entry records: a pre-merge SHA still answers the GitHub API and looks fine to anyone checking it that way, while not being reachable from a fresh clone.
records.note: Directed. Reads the clean-row conjuncts into the existential bullet as well as its universal partner, on the author's ruling that both say 'every constraint of its kind' and differ in quantifier rather than in constraint set. The asymmetry it replaces was outcome-free on revision 25: 0 of 248 vectors could discriminate the two readings, because every dirty seal there was paired with a clean witness. bad-1017 is cut to discriminate it. Positive control on the mutated line: reverting the condition moves exactly one vector and reason parity 69 -> 68.
records.reasonParityNote: Up one from 68, with the denominator grown by one. The gain is bad-1017 alone, where sealed-record-absent is now reached; the carried-record-invalid family is unchanged and still collapses three kind-keyed names the corpus distinguishes.
